transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Well, I came in because my head just doesn't stay on task anymore. It's getting in the way of things. Like, I'll be doing inventory at work, or trying to study for my supervisor certification, and I just... I keep reading the same line over and over. Or I'll walk all the way to the supply closet and completely forget what I even went in there to get. It's just been really hard to focus lately.
Have you been feeling down, losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or feeling like you're not worth much lately?

Yeah, I have. Most days, I just feel... well, like there’s this heavy, flat feeling following me around. It doesn't really matter what I'm doing. I could just be pushing my cart down an empty hallway at work, or sitting at home with my family trying to act normal, and it's still there. It's just this constant heaviness that doesn't really go away.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, even activities that usually make you happy?

I don't think so. I mean, I still like doing my usual stuff. I still enjoy hanging out with my kids or watching a game on the weekend. It's not that I don't like doing those things anymore... I just, I still have that heavy feeling while I'm doing them, if that makes sense. But the enjoyment is still there, I haven't really lost interest in it.
Have you been feeling more tired or run down lately, even if you’re not doing anything physically taxing?

Not really, no. I mean, my job keeps me on my feet a lot, so I get regular tired from that at the end of a shift. But... no, I haven't noticed feeling extra run down or exhausted when I'm just sitting around. My energy levels are mostly fine.
Have you been feeling unusually worried, restless, or on edge lately, like something bad might happen?
No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really get anxious or worried like that. It's more just... that heavy feeling I mentioned. I'm not really on edge or waiting for the other shoe to drop or anything.
Can you describe how you feel emotionally when you're spending time with your kids or watching a game on the weekend? Do you feel pleasure or satisfaction from those moments?

Yeah, I do feel pleasure from them. It's just... well, like I mentioned, most days I feel like there’s this heavy, flat feeling following me around. I can be sitting with my family, trying to act normal and enjoy the moment—and I do get satisfaction from it—but that weight is still there. It's the same everywhere, really. Even when I’m at work, just pushing my cleaning cart down an empty hallway... it's just always kind of hanging around in the background.
Is this heavy feeling something you experience most of the day, nearly every day, even when nothing stressful is happening?
Yeah, I'd say so. It's there most of the day, pretty much every day. It doesn't really matter if it's a good day or a stressful day, or if nothing at all is happening. It's just... always there.
Have you found it hard to concentrate on things, like following a conversation, reading, or making decisions?

Yeah, actually, that's a big part of why I decided to come in. My head just... it doesn't stay on task anymore. Like, I'll be doing inventory at work, or trying to study for this supervisor certification I've been looking at, and I just keep reading the same line over and over. Or I'll walk all the way to the supply closet and completely forget what I went in there for. It's just hard to keep my focus on anything.
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have slowed down, or that you feel restless or fidgety lately?

No, not really. I mean... I haven't noticed my speech slowing down or anything like that. And I don't feel restless or fidgety, either. I'm on my feet a lot for work, but I move around at a normal pace, I think. It's really just... that heavy feeling and the trouble focusing that I mentioned.
Have you been feeling like you're not worth much, or blaming yourself for things more than usual lately?

Yeah, I have. I just... I keep telling myself that other guys would have adjusted by now and moved up. But I'm still just trying not to miss the small things at work. It really makes me feel like maybe I'm just not cut out for anything more than this.
Have you noticed any days where even the things you usually enjoy, like watching a game or spending time with your kids, don't feel good at all?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I still enjoy watching a game or spending time with my kids. Those things still feel good to me. It's not like I've lost interest in the stuff I like doing... it's really just the focus issues and feeling down on myself, like I was saying before.
Have you found that you don’t take as much pleasure or interest in activities you used to enjoy, even when you're doing them?

I think that's kind of what you just asked... but no, I haven't noticed anything like that. Like I said, I still get the same enjoyment out of the things I like doing. It hasn't changed how much I care about my hobbies or anything. I'm still interested in all that stuff.
Have you been having trouble making decisions, even about small things, like what to eat or what to wear?

Well, it's not so much about deciding what to eat or wear... it's more about just keeping my head on straight. That's actually why I came in. My head just doesn't stay on task anymore. Like, I'll be doing inventory at work, or trying to study for that supervisor certification, and I just... I keep reading the same line over and over. Or I'll walk all the way to the supply closet and completely forget what I went in there for. It's just hard to think straight or focus on anything.
Would you say that your heavy or down feeling is present most of the day, nearly every day, even when you're doing things you enjoy or when there's nothing specific bothering you?

Yeah, I would say so. Most days, I just feel like there's this heavy, flat feeling that kind of follows me around. It doesn't really matter if anything specific happened or not. I could just be pushing my cleaning cart down an empty hallway at work, or sitting at home with my family just trying to act normal, and that heavy feeling is still right there with me.
Would you say that your trouble focusing or staying on task has gotten worse over time, making it harder to think clearly or get things done?

I don't think it's gotten worse, really. It's... it's just been pretty much the same for a while now. I mean, it's a constant struggle to keep my head straight at work or when I'm trying to read, but I haven't noticed it actually getting harder or anything. It just kind of stays at this same level.

Even when you're doing things you usually like, like watching a game or spending time with your kids, do you ever feel like you're just going through the motions and not really getting the same pleasure out of them as before?

No, not really. I mean, I still enjoy watching the game or hanging out with my kids. That part hasn't changed. I don't feel like I'm just going through the motions with that stuff. I still get the same enjoyment out of it as I always have. It's just that heavy feeling is still there in the background, but I still like doing the things I like.

Even when you're doing things you usually enjoy, like watching a game or spending time with your kids, do you ever feel like you can't really feel pleasure or joy, like you're just going through the motions emotionally?

Um, like I was just saying, no, not really. I don't feel numb to it or anything. I still actually feel joy when I'm with my kids or, you know, watching a game. I'm not just faking it or going through the motions emotionally. I really do feel the happiness in those moments, it's just... that heavy feeling is still kind of sitting there in the background. But I definitely still feel pleasure.

Have you noticed that, even when you're doing things you usually enjoy like watching a game or being with your kids, you don't feel as much pleasure or satisfaction from them as you used to, even if just slightly?

I feel like we're going in circles a bit here, but... no. It's exactly like I just said. I still get the exact same amount of satisfaction from my kids and from watching sports as I always did. It hasn't faded or dropped off, not even slightly.

Even when you're doing things you usually enjoy, like watching a game or spending time with your kids, do you feel like you're not able to enjoy them as much as you used to — even just a little bit — because that heavy feeling is there?

I really don't know how else to say it, Doc. No. The heavy feeling is there, yeah, but it doesn't stop me from enjoying those things. I still enjoy them just as much as I always have. It hasn't changed.
